segments.speaker: EMMA
segments.en: We’ve got to choose a topic for our experiment, haven’t we, Jack? Were you thinking of something to do with seeds?

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: That’s right. I thought we could look at seed germination – how a seed begins to grow.

segments.speaker: EMMA
segments.en: OK. Any particular reason? I know you’re hoping to work in plant science eventually ...

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Yeah, but practically everything we do is going to feed into that. No, there’s an optional module on seed structure and function in the third year that I might do, so I thought it might be useful for that [[ ]] . If I choose that option, I don’t have to do a dissertation module.

segments.speaker: EMMA
segments.en: Good idea.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Well, I thought for this experiment we could look at the relationship between seed size and the way the seeds are planted. So, we could plant different sized seeds in different ways, and see which grow best.

segments.speaker: EMMA
segments.en: OK. We’d need to allow time for the seeds to come up [[ ]] .

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: That should be fine if we start now. A lot of the other possible experiments need quite a bit longer.

segments.speaker: EMMA
segments.en: So that’d make it a good one to choose. And I don’t suppose it’d need much equipment; we’re not doing chemical analysis or anything. Though that’s not really an issue, we’ve got plenty of equipment in the laboratory.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Yeah. We need to have a word with the tutor if we’re going to go ahead with it though. I’m sure our aim’s OK. It’s not very ambitious but the assignment’s only ten percent of our final mark, isn’t it? But we need to be sure we’re the only ones doing it [[ ]] .

segments.speaker: EMMA
segments.en: Yeah, it’s only five percent actually, but it’d be a bit boring if everyone was doing it.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Did you read that book on seed germination on our reading list?

segments.speaker: EMMA
segments.en: The one by Graves? I looked through it for my last experiment, though it wasn’t all that relevant there. It would be for this experiment, though. I found it quite hard to follow – lots about the theory, which I hadn’t expected [[ ]]

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Yes, I’d been hoping for something more practical. It does include references to the recent findings on genetically-modified seeds, though.

segments.speaker: EMMA
segments.en: Yes, that was interesting.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: I read an article about seed germination by Lee Hall.

segments.speaker: EMMA
segments.en: About seeds that lie in the ground for ages and only germinate after a fire?

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: That’s the one. I knew a bit about it already, but not about this research. His analysis of figures comparing the times of the fires and the proportion of seeds that germinated was done in a lot of detail – very impressive [[ ]] .

segments.speaker: EMMA
segments.en: Was that the article with the illustrations of early stages of plant development? They were very clear.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: I think those diagrams were in another article. ———————–

segments.speaker: EMMA
segments.en: Anyway, shall we have a look at the procedure for our experiment? We’ll need to get going with it quite soon.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Right. So the first thing we have to do is find our seeds. I think vegetable seeds would be best. And obviously they mustn’t all be the same size. So, how many sorts do we need? About four different ones? [[ ]]

segments.speaker: EMMA
segments.en: I think that would be enough. There’ll be quite a large number of seeds for each one.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Then, for each seed we need to find out how much it weighs [[ ]] , and also measure its dimensions, and we need to keep a careful record of all that.

segments.speaker: EMMA
segments.en: That’ll be quite time-consuming. And we also need to decide how deep we’re going to plant the seeds [[ ]] – right on the surface, a few millimetres down, or several centimetres.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: OK. So then we get planting. Do you think we can plant several seeds together in the same plant pot? [[ ]]

segments.speaker: EMMA
segments.en: No, I think we need a different one for each seed.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Right. And we’ll need to label them – we can use different coloured labels. Then we wait for the seeds to germinate – I reckon that’ll be about three weeks, depending on what the weather’s like. Then we see if our plants have come up, and write down how tall they’ve grown. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: EMMA
segments.en: Then all we have to do is look at our numbers, and see if there’s any relation between them.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: That’s right. So ...

questions.source_text:
SECTION 3
Questions 21-30
SEED GERMINATION EXPERIMENT
Choose the correct letter A, B or C.
Questions:
    Q Num: 21
    Text: Why is Jack interested in investigating seed germination?
    Options:
        He may do a module on a related topic later on.
        He wants to have a career in plant science.
        He is thinking of choosing this topic for his dissertation.
    Q Num: 22
    Text: Jack and Emma agree the main advantage of their present experiment is that it can be
    Options:
        described very easily.
        carried out inside the laboratory.
        completed in the time available.
    Q Num: 23
    Text: What do they decide to check with their tutor?
    Options:
        whether their aim is appropriate.
        whether anyone else has chosen this topic.
        whether the assignment contributes to their final grade.
    Q Num: 24
    Text: They agree that Graves' book on seed germination is disappointing because
    Options:
        it fails to cover recent advances in seed science.
        the content is irrelevant for them.
        its focus is very theoretical.
    Q Num: 25
    Text: What does Jack say about the article on seed germination by Lee Hall?
    Options:
        The diagrams of plant development are useful.
        The analysis of seed germination statistics is thorough.
        The findings on seed germination after fires are surprising.
Stage in the experiment

A container
B soil
C weight
D condition

F colour
G types
H depths
